## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Mahāyāna *sūtra* on the right-respect etiquette of Buddhist practice, translated by **Buddhaśānta** 佛陀扇多 ([佛陀扇多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%9B%E9%99%80%E6%89%87%E5%A4%9A)) at Yè 鄴 of the Northern Wèi 元魏 in 525–539 CE. An alternate translation to [KR6k0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0117) of essentially the same Sanskrit *sūtra*.

**Abstract**

The text presents the same content as Jñānagupta's [KR6k0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0117) in an earlier Northern-Wèi recension. The double translation in two distinct Chinese renderings of the same Indian source-text indicates the importance of the Three-Jewels-etiquette tradition in early-medieval Chinese Buddhism.
